reviews.text: Before you discount the movie as a metaphysical mediation on violence, know that it is also a superbly tense thriller, and one of the most nail-bitingly effective entertainments this year.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: A film that seems headed toward one conclusion, then veers toward another over 2/₂ of the fastest-moving hours I've seen in a recent movie.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: Grim, gray and surprisingly gruesome, Prisoners - the director's first foray into English-language filmmaking - has its flaws, but predictability is not one of them.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: The plot raises complicated moral questions about how far an anguished person will go for the love of a child. At the same time, it sets up an intricate, horrifying mystery with breathtaking skill.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: "Prisoners" is a dark, deeply serious examination of how loss can unhinge us; it grabs onto you, and you may have trouble shaking it away.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: A gorgeous but manipulative thriller that wants you to ponder Big Questions as it sends a shiver down your spine.
reviews.author: Chris Vognar

reviews.text: A work of impressive craftsmanship that winds up making us think too much about how it was fashioned rather than what it has to say.
reviews.author: Ian Buckwalter

reviews.text: The screenplay is smart, the execution is impeccable, and the holes are few and far between.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: As gripping as it is grueling, with performances that swing for the fences and a knotty central mystery.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: A frustrating puzzle in which the pieces don't quite fit together
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: Even when audiences start to question the logical leaps, the performances and visuals remain first-rate. The movie doesn't feel bloated. And the final scenes are anything but a cop-out.
reviews.author: Peter Hartlaub

reviews.text: It's easy to make a thriller. It's hard to make one that says something about human nature and then, like the hauntingly compelling "Prisoners," finds something inside the genre that validates tying your nerves up in knots.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: It absorbs and controls your attention with such assurance that you hold your breath for fear of distracting the people on screen, exhaling in relief or amazement at each new revelation.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: A devastating psychological thriller, Prisoners pulls us deep into our worst fear: the Amber Alert. Then it holds us under.
reviews.author: David Hiltbrand

reviews.text: A grade-A genre exercise - but it's a genre predicated on specious reasoning and promiscuous, pseudo-sacrificial suffering.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Director Denis Villeneuve's work with the exemplary actors results in a film of startling impact, packed with twists you don't see coming. You can't shake it.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: It's a harrowing, excellent piece of work, narratively inconsistent in the final act but a film for which all flaws are easily overlooked by incredible technical accomplishments and an ensemble of performers doing close to the best work of their careers.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: If the screenplay occasionally frustrates by not asking obvious questions...and by scattering red herrings that venture into really loopy territory... the film overall works because of the filmmaking artistry and high acting calibre on display.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Throughout this beautifully made, slightly specious exercise in Old Testament revenge, the character-study aspects of "Prisoners" coexist intriguingly with the grisly-inhumanity components.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Hugh Jackman gives the performance of his career as a father seeking two kidnapped girls in Denis Villeneuve's taut thriller.
reviews.author: Betsy Sharkey

reviews.text: Villeneuve shows his sublime talents as a director who appreciates subtle dialogue and contained, intimate action.
reviews.author: Bruce Kirkland

reviews.text: Though it's nothing you haven't seen before, it's so artfully made and skillfully executed that you won't care a bit.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The final third has more in common with three-card monte street hustle than nuanced character drama.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: Seldom though does a thriller deal with such deeply disturbing, hardcore emotional distress as Prisoners.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: A very good film, with two hours of extraordinary, gripping filmmaking and twenty final minutes of subtle deflation.
reviews.author: Devin Faraci

reviews.text: It's preposterous schlock masquerading as art.
reviews.author: Joe Williams

reviews.text: Spectacular performances and a series of frighteningly tense sequences elevate it above your typical Hollywood mystery.
reviews.author: Paul Doro

reviews.text: A fascinating, skillfully directed, overpoweringly atmospheric mystery.
reviews.author: Mike Russell

reviews.text: With its measured pace and stark violence, "Prisoners" wants to be more than just an escapist crime thriller -- it has its sights set on loftier aspirations.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Easy answers are hard to come by, but that ambiguity elevates Prisoners to a place most other genre exercises rarely achieve ... or even aspire.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: Every actor in Prisoners blossoms with realistic restraint under Villeneuve's refined direction.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Prisoners uncoils with a serpent's stealth - and strikes just as suddenly.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: What makes Prisoners more potent than its oft-implausible mystery should allow is the way Villeneuve lingers over the textures of a terrible event.
reviews.author: Sam Adams

reviews.text: Great acting, in the service of a plot that keeps getting more ridiculous. I was with it until the snakes.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: A blisteringly intense master-class in suspense and character.
reviews.author: Justin Craig

reviews.text: "Prisoners" has the momentum of a thriller but it's carefully constructed so that it is also a movie that asks pointed questions about morality.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: A terrific thriller, shattering domestic drama and probing character study in a single package.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Hugh Jackman and Jake Gyllenhaal burn the candle at both ends in this emotionally whipsawing kidnapped-child thriller with an unusually strong moral resonance.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: [An] exquisitely calibrated thriller.
reviews.author: Andrea Gronvall

reviews.text: "Prisoners" is, above all, an effective thriller, but it wants you to take it more seriously than that. There's no deal-breaking reason not to.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: While the movie is certainly less than the sum of its referents, it nonetheless works as a formally controlled genre piece.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: Unflinching and intense, it's an intricate thriller evoking complex emotional conflict, moral ambiguity and sustained psychological suspense.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The script is misshapen and out of balance..Bello disappears for vast chunks of time..The rest of the cast all seem like bystanders to the Hugh and Jake show.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: Prisoners starts off promising; but peters away its substantial tension with a drawn out ending and somewhat obvious villain.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Nothing more than a cheap thriller with some pseudo-philosophical nonsense tacked on.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: It's the imitation-David Fincher pretentiousness that gets on my nerves.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: Prisoners is a dog whistle for Academy voters keyed to a pitch that screams, "For the love of God, nominate me for something!"
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: This is a powerful, engrossing film that transcends the normal constraints of its genre and is worth your investment of both time and attention.
reviews.author: Charlie McCollum

reviews.text: As a film it's edge of your seat terrifying stuff, so have at it, childless adults!
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: Prepare to be electrified! When it comes to thrillers, Prisoners is the must-see sensation of the year.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: A compelling character study of the emotional toll exacted by a kidnapping on the psyche of the victims' loved ones.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: If you're patient, and you have quite a bit of time to kill, you're bound to see beneath Prisoners' pretentious faade a nifty little crime thriller that deserved more.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: If you want to know what the families of kidnap victims go through, you can't get a better insight than by watching this film.l
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: You never sense that any of the players is inhabiting a character. Instead they seem to be dispiritedly reading lines off of an internal teleprompter ...
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: A sombrely impressive thriller in the style of Mystic River and Zodiac.
reviews.author: David Denby

reviews.text: [VIDEO ESSAY] "Prisoners" demonstrates an uncomfortable connection between criminals and their victims, whose lives take on dark aspects of their suffering. There's nothing morally comfortable.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: So sharply directed, tautly edited, rich and believably acted by Jackman and Gyllenhaal that you quickly forgive its tired story. An intense, satisfying thriller.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Please see this movie. We need to let Hollywood know that there is, in fact, an audience for sophisticated drama for adults.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: This is one hell of a movie. And yes, you can interpret that in more than a few ways.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Villeneuve is trying like hell to elevate what turns out to be a dumb genre picture...Prisoners is a long sentence.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: a movie whose execution and performances are admirable, but its eventual concession to monologuing villains and life-or-death standoffs undermines the honest and substantive character work that precedes it.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Possibly year's most immaculate-looking drivel, a prismatically shot whodunit abundant in red herrings, but lacking in moral contemplation.
reviews.author: Ed Gonzalez

reviews.text: In any case, the crowd I watched it with sat in awed, tense silence throughout-a mighty good sign that a thriller is doing its job.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: It's rooted in 40 years of Hollywood revenge films, yet it also breaks audacious new ground.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: The film is both better than you might imagine - in a doolally sort of way - and more trivial, for all its smog-like aura of utter, unremitting despair.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Prisoners offers strong drama, suspense and intrigue within a crime thriller that constantly leaves you guessing where it's going.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Intellectual torture porn.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: 'Prisoners' is the best police procedural since 'Se7en,' and it works as a grim, ugly companion piece to that film...
reviews.author: Drew McWeeny

reviews.text: It's an emotionally intense edge-of-your-seat thrill ride that won't let go of your mind, body and soul until the title card appears in the end credits.
reviews.author: Erik Davis

reviews.text: Villeneuve has produced a masterful thriller that is also an engrossing study of a smalltown America battered by recession, fear and the unrelenting elements.
reviews.author: Paul MacInnes

reviews.text: Denis Villeneuve's film requires and rewards your attention in equal measure.
reviews.author: William Goss

reviews.text: Prisoners isn't bringing much new to the tradition of crime thrillers and missing children horror stories, but it does speak mightily to how quality of craft separates an airplane page-turner from a minor work of pulp poetry.
reviews.author: Sam Woolf

reviews.text: A masterpiece. The movie everyone's going to be talking about this fall. Jackman deserves an Oscar nomination.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: 'Prisoners' is too nuanced to dismiss, but too silly to take seriously.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: A potent mix of suspense, emotion and intrigue that draws intense performances from leads Hugh Jackman and Jake Gyllenhaal.
reviews.author: John Hazelton

reviews.text: A spellbinding, sensationally effective thriller with a complex moral center that marks a grand-slam English-lingo debut for the gifted Quebecois director Denis Villeneuve.
reviews.author: Scott Foundas

reviews.text: Viewers who see the movie will find it absolutely riveting, and this is a tribute to the filmmaker's skill and to the excellent cast that brings the story to life.
reviews.author: Stephen Farber

reviews.text: Villneuve's grim chronicle of the fallout when two young girls vanish in a small town succeeds at crafting one powerfully suspenseful moment after another.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Far from the feel-good movie of the year, Prisoners is dark, disturbing, white-knuckle stuff with an unnerving shade of dread blanketed over almost every frame.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

synopsis: Keller Dover (Hugh Jackman) faces a parent's worst nightmare when his 6-year-old daughter, Anna, and her friend go missing. The only lead is an old motorhome that had been parked on their street. The head of the investigation, Detective Loki (Jake Gyllenhaal), arrests the driver (Paul Dano), but a lack of evidence forces Loki to release his only suspect. Dover, knowing that his daughter's life is at stake, decides that he has no choice but to take matters into his own hands.
